findings.title: FromContext fallback silently drops contextual attributes
findings.body: In grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext, if the underlying infra logger's FromContext does not return a *log.ConcreteLogger, the code falls back to d.New(), which returns a logger with only the original logger's context and none of the contextual attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) that ContextualLoggerMiddleware put into the request context. Since the data-egress log line in LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now depends entirely on these contextual attributes for plugin identification, this fallback would produce 'Plugin Request Completed' logs with no pluginId/endpoint, breaking log-based data egress auditing without any error or warning. Consider logging or handling the type-assertion failure explicitly.

findings.title: traceID field removed from grafana-data-egress log line
findings.body: The refactor removes the explicit "traceID" key/value pair that LoggerMiddleware previously appended to every 'Plugin Request Completed' (grafana-data-egress) log entry (tracing.TraceIDFromContext is no longer called there). Any consumer or dashboard relying on the traceID field in these data-egress logs will lose the ability to correlate egress events with traces, unless the infra logger's contextual attributes happen to include it. This is a behavioral/contract change for existing log consumers and is not called out in the PR description.

findings.title: Test and its name not updated after rename, and no tests for new middleware
findings.body: The test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware even though the middleware was renamed to MetricsMiddleware, leaving misleading test output. More importantly, the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (contextual_logger_middleware.go) has no test coverage at all: nothing verifies that endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname attributes are injected into the context for each of QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics, nor that the logger-middleware integration produces the expected log fields. Given the PR claims behavior parity (contextual logging moved rather than removed), this is a test gap.

findings.title: Comment and helper name (instrumentContext) contradict the middleware's purpose
findings.body: The comment on instrumentContext says it 'adds a contextual logger with plugin and request details to the given context', and the function retains the 'instrument' naming from the old InstrumentationMiddleware, but the function actually stores contextual log attributes via log.WithContextualAttributes, not a logger. This misleading naming/doc invites misuse; the function should be renamed (e.g. contextWithLogAttributes) and the comment corrected.

findings.title: Log fields now depend on middleware ordering, which is unenforced
findings.body: After this change, the pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname fields in the 'Plugin Request Completed' logs are supplied only by ContextualLoggerMiddleware, which must wrap (appear before) LoggerMiddleware in the middleware stack. Previously InstrumentationMiddleware was documented as 'should live at the top of the middleware stack' and the LoggerMiddleware computed these fields itself from the request. Now nothing prevents CreateMiddlewares callers or future refactors from ordering LoggerMiddleware before ContextualLoggerMiddleware, which would silently emit egress logs missing all identifying fields. The old comment about the required stack position was dropped instead of being moved to the new middleware, so the ordering constraint is now undocumented.
